Aisha (Support): FYI ACME reporting a big p99 latency spike starting ~15:10 UTC, they see multiple API errors and tails near 5-8s. Customer noticed message: \"request failed: internal server error (alloc failure)\". Ticket 8672 attached.
Raj (Eng-SRE): Can you paste the tenant id + a sample trace? Also which model and region?
Aisha (Support): tenant=acme-prod-11, model=redwood-3b-q4_0, region=us-west2. Trace excerpt: `500 internal: alloc failed - oom during kv growth`
Customer (ACME): Confirming we started seeing this around 15:07 UTC after a burst of traffic from a nightly job. We had ~300 concurrent streaming requests for long contexts (~2048).
Priya (Runtime): That pattern smells like KV cache growth + fragmentation. Need GPU slab stats, per-worker kv_size, and allocator warnings. Can you run: ```kubectl -n inference logs -l app=worker -c runtime | grep -E \"KV_CACHE|Allocator|OOM|slab\" -A3 -B1```
Aisha (Support): Ran that, here's the snippet: ```[15:09:21] KV_CACHE grow tenant=acme-prod-11 from=1.2GB to=3.8GB
[15:09:22] Allocator WARN: slab_alloc failed size=128MB try=3
[15:09:22] OOM: gpu0 alloc failed at 0x7ff... requested=256MB
[15:09:23] Worker restart scheduled to recover```
SRE-Bot: ALERT: high_gpu_mem_pressure tenant=acme-prod-11 p99_latency=7.8s p95_latency=3.2s gpu_util=72% free_mem=600MB
Raj (Eng-SRE): OK. Immediate triage: 1) throttle or route ACME to a lower-throughput pool 2) reduce per-request max_tokens or context length 3) enable active fallback to cpu/cheaper model if present. Can support shift traffic?
Mike (Support-Infra): I can reroute them to the burst pool if we accept higher cost. Also suggest temporarily lowering default batch_size for their route to 1 to reduce KV growth. Want me to flip a config?
Aisha (Support): Please flip the route batch_size -> 1 and enable active_fallback=true. Doing so now. Will monitor.
Priya (Runtime): Longer term fix: we saw allocator fragmentation in 1.2.4; 1.3.0 has a slab compaction pass and a per-tenant kv-cap limiter. Can we schedule a kernel upgrade for their workers? Also upload heap snapshot from `runtime/metrics/slab_stats` and `kv/usage` 
Raj (Eng-SRE): Steps to repro (from customer): ```for i in $(seq 1 300); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @long_ctx.json & done``` That reproduces ramp and kv growth. We should repro in staging with synthetic tenant to validate allocator patch.
Aisha (Support): After lowering batch_size and enabling fallback, their p99 dropped to ~1.4s within 6 minutes. Customer confirmed improved experience. :thumbsup:
Customer (ACME): Thanks — noticeable improvement. Please keep us posted on root cause and permanent mitigation.
Priya (Runtime): Action items: - capture slab_stats and kv snapshots from affected workers (paths: /var/log/runtime/slab_stats.log, /var/log/runtime/kv_usage.log) - run allocator debug dump: `rd-allocator dump --tenant acme-prod-11 > /tmp/dump.json` - reproduce in staging with same concurrency and context.
Raj (Eng-SRE): Short-term mitigations tracked: 1) route change (Mike) 2) batch_size->1 (Mike) 3) active_fallback enabled (Aisha) 4) temporary quota throttle (Aisha)
Mike (Support-Infra): Done: route switch + batch_size change at 15:20 UTC. Logs: `route:update acme-prod-11 batch_size=1 fallback=true`
SRE-Bot: NOTE: job allocator-defrag scheduled on worker-pool-3 at 15:45 UTC (non-disruptive background compaction)
Priya (Runtime): Proposed permanent fixes: enable per-tenant KV caps (config `kv.max_per_tenant=2GB`), land allocator 1.3.0 with slab compaction, add eviction policy tuned for long-context streaming, and add a health check that triggers fallback before OOM.
Aisha (Support): Customer asked about a timeline for permanent fix. Priya, can we schedule a canary for next week?
Priya (Runtime): I'll prepare a canary with allocator 1.3.0 in staging tomorrow, run the 300-concurrent repro for 30m, collect metrics. If green, roll to prod week after.
Raj (Eng-SRE): Postmortem checklist: collect worker heap dumps, KV growth heatmap, request traces for 15:00-15:30, config diffs, and confirm no other tenants affected. Assigning owners: Priya (runtime) for patch + canary, Raj (sre) for heatmap and postmortem, Mike (infra) for routing playbook updates, Aisha to keep customer updated.
Mike (Support-Infra): Quick note: in future we can also autoscale worker pool for short-lived KV spikes to avoid tail risk. Need cost/benefit analysis.
Aisha (Support): I'll send ACME a summary and ETA. Thanks everyone.
Priya (Runtime): Thanks — saved the logs under /mnt/triage/acme/1795558888/ and started the canary branch `allocator-1.3-canary`.
Raj (Eng-SRE): Leaving this thread open until postmortem is posted. Close when PMT has reviewed. :eyes:
